headline: High-risk editor-to-data-engineering pairing: Cursor’s default filesystem/network/tool access can create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; RisingWave adds no compensating isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP/tool outputs by default, so attacker-controlled content can steer its agent loop. RisingWave is not an interactive agent, but if Cursor opens or copies RisingWave-controlled content, the shared local filesystem/clipboard bridge makes injection plausible. No direct evidence of a hardened provenance boundary is present.
conditions: IF Cursor opens untrusted RisingWave files or buffers as instructions
IF clipboard content from one agent is pasted into the other without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff for agent outputs
Keep RisingWave artifacts in a read-only directory
Use separate workspaces per agent
Require explicit human review before Cursor executes instructions from files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared-file content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor can read workspace files and send content to model providers and MCP servers, while RisingWave is open-source and network-egress none. If sensitive data is present in the shared filesystem, Cursor may transmit it off-box; RisingWave does not offset that risk. The pair therefore has a default leakage path through Cursor, even though RisingWave itself is local.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened in Cursor’s workspace
IF Cursor routes file contents to a third-party model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared workspace
Use a separate non-sensitive repo for Cursor
Turn off MCP servers for sensitive sessions
Restrict model-provider access to redacted inputs
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has unrestricted filesystem write, git modification, shell execution, and broad network egress; RisingWave is a database/stream-processing system with no stated coordination or locking surface. If both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git-state changes can collide and corrupt work. Uncertainty about RisingWave’s runtime coordination means the safer higher severity is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same working tree or git branch
IF RisingWave artifacts are modified while Cursor auto-runs commands in Yolo mode
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Avoid Yolo mode on shared repos
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level write arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can act on generated content, and its tool-use pattern allows multi-step execution; RisingWave provides no verification layer or downstream check. If Cursor produces incorrect code or commands and the other side consumes them as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits, shell actions, or bad data-engineering changes. The interaction is plausible in default workflows, so high is justified.
conditions: IF Cursor-generated output is copied into RisingWave-related code or configs without review
IF Cursor auto-runs commands based on its own prior outputs
mitigations: Require human review before applying generated diffs
Use a second-pass validator for commands and SQL
Disable auto-run for risky sessions
Limit Cursor to read-only analysis on critical tasks
requires-engineering: add output verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor’s docs indicate broad network egress and third-party model-provider calls, which can create residency or retention concerns if regulated data is opened. RisingWave itself is open-source with no documented data-handling constraints here, so the compliance risk is mainly on Cursor’s side. No specific mismatch is evidenced for RisingWave, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in Cursor while third-party model providers are enabled
IF organizational policy forbids off-box processing of the touched data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cursor sessions
Use local-only models for sensitive work
Review vendor privacy settings before use
Separate compliant and non-compliant projects
requires-engineering: formalize residency controls
